entities.name: Poncello Orsini
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Poncello Orsini (died February 10, 1395) was a prominent Italian cardinal and scion of the powerful Roman Orsini family, whose ecclesiastical career was deeply entangled with the tumultuous politics of the late 14th century, particularly the Western Schism. Elevated to cardinal by Pope Urban VI in 1378, Orsini's allegiance to the Roman pontiff against the Avignon antipopes positioned him as a critical figure in the struggle for papal legitimacy, shaping the early decades of the Schism. His influence stemmed not only from his cardinalatial office but also from the immense temporal power and extensive networks commanded by the Orsini clan within the Papal States.

Orsini's career began with his appointment as administrator of the Diocese of Aversa in 1370, becoming its bishop in 1378, the same year he received the red hat as Cardinal-Priest of San Clemente. This elevation occurred just weeks after the election of Clement VII as antipope, thrusting Orsini into the heart of the schism. He remained a staunch supporter of Urban VI, participating actively in the Roman Curia and leveraging his family's considerable resources to buttress the Roman papacy's authority amidst widespread defections. He played a consultative role in curial affairs and was present at the papal conclave of 1389, which successfully elected Boniface IX, further solidifying the Roman line of succession.

His unwavering commitment to the Roman papacy contributed to the eventual stabilization of the Roman line during the Western Schism, even as the broader conflict persisted for decades after his death. The Orsini family, through Poncello and other clerical members, continued to exert significant influence over the Papal States and the broader Church hierarchy, illustrating the enduring power of aristocratic dynasties in shaping medieval ecclesiastical institutions. His actions helped to maintain the organizational integrity of the Roman Church during a period of profound fragmentation.

His actions, backed by the powerful Orsini family, helped prevent an even deeper fragmentation of the Church's authority.
